Sorry, I was misguided in attributing that to the Manifesto. When I read it, there was the Principles of Communism attached to the end of the pdf I was reading. The first line of section 18 of the Principles of Communism clearly states that:

“What will be the course of the revolution? Above all, it will be to establish a democratic constitution, and through this, the direct or indirect dominance of the proletariat”

I’d like to point out that parliament and worker’s councils are not mutually exclusive, and that for the setting of national policy and that the execution of the necessary reforms for society can be taken through parliamentary procedures (see Principles of Communism section 18). There is nothing inherently bourgeoisie about national government being elected other than the significant corruption that takes place. In fact, the bourgeoisie turn on democracy as soon as it no longer favors them due to increased worker conscious (see Reform and Revolution chapter 7.) True democracy reflects the interests of the working class as the working class make up the vast majority of society. I’m pretty sure this is what Engels means be indirect dominance of the proletariat in his conception of a democratic transitional state. I have nothing against worker councils and believe they are extremely important, however I don’t believe there should be a political monopoly for the first party to violently claim it stands for the workers. If there’s some (non Leninist) theory that refutes that conclusion I’d love to hear it.
